title: Progressive Cavity Pump

introduction.definition: A progressive cavity (PC) pump has a single-helix metal rotor turning eccentrically inside a double-helix elastomer stator. The rotor and stator form sealed cavities that progress from suction to discharge without changing shape, so the pump moves viscous, shear-sensitive and solids-laden liquids gently with a smooth flow.
applications: Alumina: flocculant dosing and thickener underflow (selected duties)
key_points: Flow ∝ speed; pressure capability ∝ number of stages (≈ 6 bar per stage typical)
Never run dry — the stator burns

classification.configuration: Progressive cavity (Moineau), 1:2 rotor/stator lobe geometry, 2 stages

introduction.summary: A single-helix steel rotor turns inside a double-helix rubber stator. Because the stator pitch is twice the rotor pitch, a chain of sealed cavities forms along the pump; as the rotor turns (rolling eccentrically, its axis orbiting the stator axis), the cavities progress from suction to discharge without changing shape or volume. The result is smooth, low-shear, nearly pulse-free flow proportional to speed — ideal for sludges, pastes, viscous and shear-sensitive products, and liquids with solids or gas.

what_to_look_for: The rotor turns eccentrically inside the stator, driven through a connecting rod with universal joints.
Sealed cavities form at the suction end and fill with liquid.
The cavities progress along the stator to the discharge without changing volume.

steps.text: The rotor turns eccentrically inside the stator, driven through a connecting rod with universal joints.
Sealed cavities form at the suction end and fill with liquid.
The cavities progress along the stator to the discharge without changing volume.
The interference fit between rotor and stator seals the cavities; more stages hold more pressure.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Flow almost linear with speed; slip increases with pressure and decreases with viscosity.

piping: Size the suction line for low velocity (viscous liquids need large suction pipes); provide a strainer.
Fit a pressure-relief valve (integral or in the discharge line) — a positive-displacement pump will build pressure until something breaks if the discharge is blocked.
Support piping independently of the pump.
Leave space to remove the stator from the rotor (pull-out length).
commissioning: Never start against a closed discharge valve.
Fill the pump with liquid (or ensure the suction is flooded) before start — avoid dry running unless the design allows it.
Dry-run protection (temperature or flow sensor in the stator).

periodic.task: Inspect universal joints and their sleeves.

overhaul.task: Replace stator when slip rises; check rotor chrome plating.

lubrication: Joints grease-filled and sealed by sleeves.

video_tutorials.title: Progressive Cavity Pump — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Progressive Cavity Pump.
A progressive cavity (PC) pump has a single-helix metal rotor turning eccentrically inside a double-helix elastomer stator.

The rotor and stator form sealed cavities that progress from suction to discharge without changing shape, so the pump moves viscous, shear-sensitive and solids-laden liquids gently with a smooth flow.
Typical applications include wastewater sludge and polymer dosing; food (fruit pulp, dough); oil-field and mining slurries; paper, paint and adhesives.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Suction Housing, Discharge Flange (End Housing), Stator Tie Rods, Drive Shaft.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Progressive Cavity Pump — Operation

script.narration: How the Progressive Cavity Pump works.
The rotor turns eccentrically inside the stator, driven through a connecting rod with universal joints.
Sealed cavities form at the suction end and fill with liquid.
The cavities progress along the stator to the discharge without changing volume.
The interference fit between rotor and stator seals the cavities; more stages hold more pressure.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

video_tutorials.title: Progressive Cavity Pump — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Progressive Cavity Pump.
Check discharge pressure and seal.
Inspect universal joints and their sleeves.
Replace stator when slip rises; check rotor chrome plating.
Watch for dry running stator burn: rubber smell, rapid flow loss. Common cause: empty suction.
Watch for stator wear / swelling: flow loss or high torque. Common cause: abrasives; chemical incompatibility; temperature.
Watch for joint failure: knocking. Common cause: torn sleeve, lost grease.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.

questions.question: What determines the pressure a PC pump can develop?
questions.explanation: Each stage holds roughly the same pressure.

questions.question: Why must a PC pump not run dry?
options: The elastomer stator overheats and burns

questions.question: Why is a PC pump good for shear-sensitive liquids?
options: Cavities move gently without changing shape

questions.question: What allows the rotor to orbit eccentrically while the drive shaft turns concentrically?
options: Connecting rod with universal (or flexible) joints
